Georgia Power Company’s 
Semi-Annual Nuclear Uprate Report



Reporting Period End Date: December 31, 2025








Project Background
This Semi-Annual Nuclear Uprate Report (“Report”) provides the status of the Extended Power Uprates (“EPUs”) at Plant Vogtle Units 1-2 (“Plant Vogtle”) and Plant Hatch Units 1-2 (“Plant Hatch”). This Report is filed pursuant to the Georgia Public Service Commission’s (the “Commission”) Order Adopting Stipulation, dated July 31, 2025, (the “Order”) in Georgia Power Company’s (“Georgia Power” or the “Company”) 2025 Integrated Resource Plan (“2025 IRP”), Docket No. 56002.  

EPU is a validated, proven process that has been implemented previously at Plant Hatch and Plant Vogtle, and by other nuclear electric utility operators, that delivers incremental capacity and energy gains. The objective of the EPU process is to increase thermal power (where the reactor produces more heat) to increase steam pressure and flow to the turbine generators, thus producing higher electrical output from the units without using additional fuel. The process includes an extensive analysis of plant systems and components to verify the capability of the EPUs and identify the modifications needed to support the power upgrade at each facility. 

The EPU projects will modify key components of the units, including turbines, generators, large pumps and motors, and cooling systems, to allow the units to safely and reliably produce more electricity. Many of the modifications will replace existing components that are contemplated for future end-of-life replacement to enhance performance, and some will create incremental capacity gains from the increased thermal output of the EPU implementation. The Company identifies components as end-of-life when the component is expected to be replaced within the expected operating life of the plant. The EPU components include:

Turbine Upgrade: The high-pressure (“HP”) turbine will be upgraded to handle the increased steam flow and pressure. HP turbines are the first to receive steam and experience the highest temperatures and pressures. 
Steam Cycle Upgrades:
Feedwater Heaters: (Hatch only) Preheat water entering the reactor, improving efficiency of the water heating process in the reactor.
Moisture Separator Reheaters (MSRs): (Vogtle 1-2 only) Remove water droplets from the steam and reheat the steam before it enters the Low-pressure turbines, thus protecting the turbines and improving efficiency.
Steam Dryers: (Hatch only) Remove moisture from the steam, like MSRs. Upgrading steam dryers ensures high steam quality and improves turbine efficiency and reliability under increased steam flow conditions.
Condensate Pumps and Motors: (Hatch only) Move condensed steam from the condenser to the feedwater system. Upgrading will improve efficiency and ensure proper flows and pressures for the feedwater system.
Cooling Tower / Circulating Water: Provides an energy efficient way of removing heat from water that circulates through the condenser. Adding cooling towers, replacing fill material, and/or upgrading circulating water pumps will accommodate additional steam produced after the EPUs.
Generator Upgrade: The generator will be upgraded to handle the increased power output. Upgrades to the exciter and/or rotor are needed for increased generation.
Maximum Extended Load Line Limit Analysis Plus (MELLLA+): (Hatch Only) Expands the power/flow map to provide more operating flexibility for uprated plants to achieve full core thermal power.

Key Updates (July 1, 2025 – December 31, 2025)
General Progress Update
Schedule development for EPU project implementation made significant progress through the year. This progress has developed further confidence and reduced risk in the ability to complete the engineering analysis, licensing, and implementation periods as designed. 
Plant Vogtle 1-2
Engineering Status
Westinghouse Engineering (“Westinghouse”) analysis Step 1, Feasibility Engineering Analysis, was initiated April 2024 and completed October 2024. Step 2 of 3, Preliminary Engineering Study of the incremental capacity uprate, commenced with Westinghouse in November 2024 and is on track for completion in March 2026. This phase further refines the project scope that supports the uprate. Preparation of the License Amendment Request (“LAR”) for the fuel transition is targeted for submittal to the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (“NRC”) in the third quarter of 2027, with the uprate LAR planned for submittal to the NRC during the first quarter of 2029. Contract status details are included in Attachment 1.   
On-going Vendor Equipment Testing
As of December 31, 2025, Southern Nuclear Company (“SNC”) continues working with its vendors to perform factory acceptance testing to evaluate the upgraded rating of the step-up transformers associated with the uprate project. Testing is scheduled to conclude by June 2026.
Updated Incremental Capacity Gains
The vendor has provided updated efficiency projections that now range from 23-24 MW per unit (GPC 46.8% ownership), representing a 13.0% decrease from what was initially projected in the Company’s 2025 Integrated Resource Plan. During the engineering analysis, an issue was identified with increasing the temperature of the reactor coolant system that would present a long-term vulnerability to the Steam Generators. Accordingly, it was determined to target a lower temperature increase to mitigate that risk. The lower temperature increase target results in lower total MW gains per unit.  
Plant Hatch 1-2
Engineering Status
Engineering analysis for the incremental capacity uprates began with GE Vernova Hitachi Nuclear Energy in August 2025 and remains on schedule for completion in October 2027. This phase confirms the scope and prepares the documentation for the LAR. Currently, the LAR is scheduled for submittal to the NRC in the third quarter of 2027. Contract status details are provided in Attachment 2.
Updated Efficiency Projections
Current projected efficiency gains from the upgraded HP turbines are slightly below earlier estimates and now range from 23-26 MW per unit (GPC 50.1% ownership), representing a 15.7% decrease from what was initially projected in the Company’s 2025 Integrated Resource Plan. Heat balance analyses to validate these assumptions are underway and scheduled for completion in March 2026. 
Necessary Component Replacements
As a part of the engineering development of the Hatch 1-2 EPU project, SNC and vendor analysis of the HP Turbine and 4th Stage Feedwater Heaters identified that the existing components are degraded beyond Company management margin expectations and require replacement within the next several years. Accordingly, the Company has made the decision to move forward with procuring these assets for implementation during upcoming refueling outages.
